Basketball Stats, Height, Age |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/players/296336-georges-maguette-niang |website=FIBA Basketball |access-date=1 November 2025}} ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|n|iː|æ|ŋ}} {{respell|NEE|ang}};{{cite press release |author= |title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide |publisher=National Basketball Association |date=October 24, 2023 |access-date=May 17, 2024}} born June 17, 1993), nicknamed "'''the Minivan'''" and "'''G Wagon'''" is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Golden State Warriors]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He was an [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] college player for the [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State Cyclones]]. ==Early life== Niang is the son of Sidy and Alison Niang. His father was born and raised in Senegal.{{cite web |date=March 23, 2017 |title=Niang veut jouer pour le Sénégal |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/fr/afrobasketqualifiers/2017/news/niang-keen-to-play-for-senegal-at-fiba-afrobasket-2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170823141149/http://www.fiba.basketball/fr/afrobasketqualifiers/2017/news/niang-keen-to-play-for-senegal-at-fiba-afrobasket-2017 |archive-date=August 23, 2017 |access-date=July 14, 2017 |work=FIBA.com |language=fr}} He was elected student body president at Tilton Prep.{{Cite web |title=Georges Niang - Men's Basketball |url=https://cyclones.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/georges-niang/6525 |access-date=2022-02-09 |website=Iowa State University Athletics |language=en}} ==High school career== A three-year starter and two-year team captain, Niang capped off his career as one of the greatest players in the [[Tilton School]] history, amassing a school-record 2,372 points. He was a three-time First-Team All-NEPSAC Class AA pick, Niang was the 2012 NEPSAC Class AA Player of the Year.{{cite web |title=2011 - 2012 NEPSAC Boys' Basketball All-New England Selections |url=http://nepsac.org/page/3086/article/748 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151210212514/http://www.nepsac.org/page/3086/article/748 |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 10, 2015 |access-date=July 30, 2014 |website=NEPSAC.org}} He averaged 25.1 points, 7.2 rebounds, and 2.1 assists per game as a senior, averaged 24.2 points and 8.2 rebounds as a junior and led his team to the 2011 NEPSAC Class AA championship with a 72–56 win over St. Mark's. He was named outstanding player of the tournament, scoring 23 points on 11-of-11 shooting from the field in the championship game. His team lost in the 2011 National Prep Championship to Notre Dame Prep (87–85), as Niang scored 31 points.{{cite web |last=Finkelstein |first=Adam |date=March 10, 2011 |title=National Prep Championship recap |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/news/story?id=6201933 |access-date=November 2, 2024 |website=ESPN.com}} He played for the [[Boston]]-based BABC AAU team, the same program that featured former [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Cyclone]] and NBA player [[Will Blalock]]. His BABC squad won the 2011 Nike Peach Jam, one of the most competitive AAU tournaments in the country.{{cite web|first=Ian|last=Powers|title=2011 Nike Peach Jam: Top Prospects|url=http://www.nbadraft.net/2011-nike-peach-jam-top-prospects|website=NBADraft.net|date=July 19, 2011|access-date=July 30, 2014}} He was teammates at Tilton and in AAU with [[Nerlens Noel]], they won four NEPSAC titles, one national prep championship, one AAU national championship and one [[Nike EYBL]] title in his career. Niang was considered one of the best players on the East Coast, ending his prep career as a consensus national top-100 recruit. He was ranked No. 42 by Lindy's, No. 56 by [[ESPNU]],{{cite web |title=Georges Niang recruiting profile |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/102752 |access-date=July 30, 2014 |website=ESPN.com}} No. 69 by [[Scout.com]], No. 69 by [[Rivals.com]],{{cite web|title=Georges Niang profile|url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/maple/117208|website=Rivals.com|access-date=July 30, 2014}} No. 73 by [[The Sporting News]], and No. 81 by [[CBS Sports]] in the 2012 prep national rankings. He also had offers from [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]], [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence]], [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]] and [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]], eventually committing to [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]]. {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2011}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Georges Niang | position = [[Forward (basketball)|F]] | hometown = [[Methuen, MA]] | highschool = [[Tilton School]] (NH) | feet = 6 | inches = 8 | weight = 210 | 40 = | commitdate = May 5, 2011 | scout stars = 4 | rivals stars = 4 | 247 stars = 4 | espn stars = 4 }} {{College athlete recruit end | 40 = | year = 2012 | rivals ref title = Iowa State 2012 Basketball Commitments | espn ref title = ESPN | rivals school = iowastate | espn schoolid = 66 | rivals overall = 6, 16 (F) | espn overall = 56, 2 (NH), 14 (F) | accessdate = June 14, 2015 | bball = yes }} ==College career== [[File:Big 12 Championship (25772775155) (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|160px|Niang playing for Iowa State]] Niang was named to the [[Big 12]] All-Rookie Team in his freshman year in 2013. In the second round of the [[2014 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2014 NCAA tournament]], Niang broke the [[Fifth metatarsal bone|fifth metatarsal]] in his right foot, forcing him to sit for the remainder of the event.{{cite web |title=Georges Niang Bio |url=https://cyclones.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/georges-niang/6525 |access-date=November 2, 2024 |website=Cyclones.com}} As a sophomore, he averaged 16.7 points and 4.5 rebounds as the third-most-prominent offensive weapon for Iowa State behind [[Melvin Ejim]] and [[DeAndre Kane]].{{cite news |last=Forgrave |first=Reid |date=October 17, 2014 |title=Gorgeous Georges? Iowa State's Niang will look a lot different this season |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/college-basketball/gorgeous-georges-iowa-states-niang-will-look-a-lot-different-this-season |access-date=November 2, 2024 |work=[[Fox Sports]]}} Niang cut back on his calorie consumption in the 2014 offseason and consequently slimmed down to {{Convert|230|lb}} from {{Convert|260|lb}}. As a junior, Niang led the team in scoring with 15.3 points per game to go along with 5.4 rebounds and 3.4 assists per game. Seeded third in the [[2015 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2015 NCAA tournament]], the Cyclones were upset by 14th-seeded [[2014–15 UAB Blazers men's basketball team|UAB]] in the round of 64 despite 11 points and seven rebounds from Niang. He considered entering the [[2015 NBA draft]], but instead decided to return for his senior season. "I was weighing it, but I want to be loyal to the program and didn't want to go out this way," Niang said. "I didn't want to leave my mark like that."{{cite magazine |date=March 30, 2015 |title=Iowa State's Georges Niang says he's returning next season |url=https://www.si.com/college/2015/03/30/iowa-state-georges-niang-returning-senior-season |access-date=November 2, 2024 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]}} Niang surpassed the 2,000-point threshold as a senior, averaging 20.2 points and 6.2 rebounds per game.{{Cite web |date=February 17, 2016 |title=Men's Basketball: Niang overtakes Hoiberg, hits 2,000-point mark |url=http://amestrib.com/sports/men-s-basketball-niang-overtakes-hoiberg-hits-2000-point-mark |access-date=February 17, 2016 |website=Amestrib.com |archive-date=February 22, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160222085816/http://amestrib.com/sports/men-s-basketball-niang-overtakes-hoiberg-hits-2000-point-mark |url-status=dead }} He was named to the 35-man midseason watchlist for the [[Naismith College Player of the Year]] on February 11.{{cite news|last=Payne|first=Terrence|title=Naismith Trophy midseason list announced|url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/oklahoma-sooners-buddy-hield-lsu-tigers-ben-simmons-naismith-trophy-35-finalists-021116|work=[[Fox Sports]]|date=February 11, 2016|access-date=February 19, 2016}} During his college career, Niang achieved a number of program records, including the first player to reach four straight NCAA tournaments, the first two-time All-American, the career leader in games played (138) and most wins (98).{{cite news |last=Montz |first=Dylan |date=March 16, 2016 |title=Georges Niang era at Iowa State produced numerous milestones |url=http://www.thegazette.com/subject/sports/college/mens-basketball/georges-niang-era-at-iowa-state-produced-numerous-milestones-20160326 |work=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids)]]}} ==Professional career== ===Indiana Pacers (2016–2017)=== On June 23, 2016, Niang was selected by the [[Indiana Pacers]] with the 50th overall pick in the [[2016 NBA draft]].{{cite web |last=Taylor |first=Nate |date=June 24, 2016 |title=Pacers select Georges Niang in 2nd round of NBA draft |url=http://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2016/06/24/pacers-select-georges-niang-2nd-round-nba-draft/86323740/ |access-date=December 15, 2016 |work=IndyStar.com}} He joined the team for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]], where his early play drew praise from [[Larry Bird]].{{cite web|url=http://www.eagletribune.com/sports/local_sports/nba-summer-league-niang-earns-praise-from-bird/article_d96c032e-6f98-52e7-b229-4aba84fb0101.html|title=NBA Summer League; Niang earns praise from Bird|work=EagleTribune.com|date=July 5, 2016|access-date=July 5, 2016}} On July 11, 2016, he signed with the Pacers.{{cite web |date=July 11, 2016 |title=Georges Niang Signs with Pacers |url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/georges-niang-signs-pacers |access-date=July 11, 2016 |work=NBA.com}} During his rookie season, he had multiple assignments with the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] of the [[NBA Development League]].{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|title=2016-17 NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=February 7, 2017|archive-date=January 26, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170126075350/http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|url-status=dead}} On July 14, 2017, he was waived by the Pacers.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/pacers-waive-georges-niang|title=Pacers Waive Georges Niang|work=NBA.com|date=July 14, 2017|access-date=July 14, 2017}} ===Santa Cruz Warriors (2017–2018)=== On August 16, 2017, Niang signed an Exhibit 10 contract with the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{Cite web |last=Chiari |first=Mike |date=August 16, 2017 |title=Georges Niang Reportedly Signs Warriors Contract, Will 'Likely' Play in G-League |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2727749-georges-niang-reportedly-signs-warriors-contract-will-likely-play-in-g-league |access-date=April 9, 2022 |website=Bleacher Report}} He was waived by the Warriors on October 14, 2017.{{Cite web |last=Letourneau |first=Connor |date=October 13, 2017 |title=Warriors waive Michael Gbinije, Georges Niang |url=https://www.sfgate.com/warriors/article/Warriors-waive-Michael-Gbinije-Georges-Niang-12277748.php |access-date=April 9, 2022 |website=SFGate}} He subsequently joined the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] as an affiliate player. ===Utah Jazz (2018–2021)=== On January 14, 2018, Niang signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Utah Jazz]] to take up a spot previously held by former college teammate [[Naz Mitrou-Long]].{{Cite web |date=January 14, 2018 |title=Jazz Sign Georges Niang to Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/jazz-sign-georges-niang-two-way-contract |access-date=April 9, 2022 |website=NBA}} Throughout the rest of the season, he split his playing time between the Jazz and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Salt Lake City Stars]]. On July 13, 2018, Niang signed a standard contract with the Jazz.{{cite web |title=Jazz Sign Forward Georges Niang |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-sign-forward-georges-niang |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 15, 2018 |date=July 13, 2018}} Niang scored a then-career-high 24 points against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] on April 10, 2019. He also notched a 24-point game against the [[Houston Rockets]] on May 8, 2021.{{cite web |last=Falk |first=Aaron |date=May 8, 2021 |title=Georges Niang ties career high as the Utah Jazz handle the Houston Rockets |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/georges-niang-ties-career-high-utah-jazz-handle-houston-rockets |access-date=June 5, 2021 |website=NBA.com}} ===Philadelphia 76ers (2021–2023)=== [[File:Georges Niang (51827355728) (cropped).jpg|thumb|Niang with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in 2022]] On August 9, 2021, Niang signed a two-year, $6.7 million contract with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web |last=Seltzer |first=Brian |date=August 9, 2021 |title=76ers Sign Georges Niang |url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/76ers-sign-georges-niang |access-date=November 2, 2024 |work=NBA.com}}{{cite news |last=Levick |first=Noah |title=Source: Power forward Niang agrees to 2-year deal with Sixers |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/sixers/nba-free-agency-georges-niang-sixers-utah-jazz-nba-offseason |access-date=8 October 2021 |work=NBC Sports Philadelphia |date=3 August 2021}} With the team, he carried over the "Minivan" nickname he maintained in Utah.{{cite news |last=Jones |first=Tony |title=Now with the 76ers, Georges 'The Minivan' Niang is rolling up to Utah, the place that gave him his NBA start |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2955784/2021/11/16/now-with-the-76ers-georges-the-minivan-niang-is-rolling-up-to-utah-the-place-that-gave-him-his-nba-start/ |access-date=16 November 2021 |work=The Athletic |date=25 December 2022}} His time with the 76ers accounted for his most sizable role - backing up forward [[Tobias Harris]] among others - and points per game to that point in his career. Niang had his highest scoring output as a Sixer on April 7, 2023, posting 24 points in a 136–131 overtime win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]] on 5-7 shooting from 3.{{Cite web |date=April 7, 2023 |title=76ers rest all 5 starters, still beat Hawks 136-131 in OT |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401469360 |access-date=March 6, 2025 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}} ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2023–2025)=== On July 6, 2023, Niang signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases-niang-jerome-signing-230706|title=Cavaliers Sign Georges Niang and Ty Jerome|work=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2023}} On January 17, 2024, Niang scored a new career high of 33 points against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], making 13 of his 14 shots attempts.{{Cite web |date=2024-01-18 |title=Georges Niang near perfect, Cavs offense lights up Rocket Mortage FieldHouse in 135-95 win over Bucks |url=https://www.news5cleveland.com/sports/basketball/cavaliers/george-niang-near-perfect-cavs-offense-lights-up-rocket-mortage-fieldhouse-in-135-95-win-over-bucks |access-date=2024-01-25 |website=News 5 Cleveland WEWS |language=en}} In the [[2023-24 NBA season]] Niang played 82 games, averaging 9.4 points per game.{{Cite web |title=Georges Niang {{!}} Cleveland Cavaliers |url=https://www.nba.com/player/1627777/georges-niang/ |access-date=2024-04-22 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} ===Atlanta Hawks (2025)=== On February 6, 2025, Niang, along with [[Caris LeVert]], three second-round picks, and two pick swaps were traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in exchange for [[De'Andre Hunter]].{{Cite web|title=Atlanta Hawks Complete Trade with Cleveland Cavaliers|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-complete-trade-with-cleveland-cavaliers|date=2025-02-06|access-date=2025-02-07|website=NBA.com|language=en}} === Golden State Warriors Hawks, and [[Terance Mann]] and the draft rights to [[Drake Powell]] (the 22nd pick in the [[2025 NBA draft]]) to the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web | title=Celtics Complete Trades with Portland and
